title: A goal reports which required variables are unset, and the repository lists their names in .env.example
description:
SPIDR grandchild C of task-72b22fcf9da54b3b91dabf5b7392aff1 (architect-aa54e231, 2026-09-05). Owns the parent's DoD 3 and 4. dependsOn grandchild B task-fd2d438f29d64830a2bd6110f2ded78b, which adds the field this row READS - without it there are no names to report, and the parent's DoD 3 is unsatisfiable (measured: no variable-name field exists on a deployment requirement anywhere).

Deliberately does NOT depend on grandchild A: the unset report needs the NAMES of what is set, which the existing read already returns as metadata (apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-store.ts `readEnvironmentVariables`), not the plaintext values A delivers. A and C can run in parallel.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: reading the required names off the approved contract, reporting which are unset for a given environment, and putting those names into the repository's `.env.example`.

`.env.example` ALREADY EXISTS AND ALREADY CARRIES VALUES - this is the trap and it is measured, not guessed. It is generated by the CONTROLLED-PROFILE generator, not by the node lander the parent's description names:
  apps/daemon/src/repository/controlled-profile/controlled-profile-root-templates.ts:204 maps `.env.example` to an ENV_EXAMPLE template, whose current content includes a real placeholder value (`POSTGRES_PASSWORD=...`, and README copy at :113 telling the operator to `cp .env.example .env   # then replace every CHANGE_ME`).
  apps/daemon/src/repository/controlled-profile/controlled-profile-generator.test.ts:32 pins the file by SHA256 in a golden manifest - editing the template MOVES that hash and the pin must move with it.
  apps/daemon/src/repository/deployment/deployment-infrastructure-generator.test.ts:305-306 READS a placeholder back out of `.env.example` with `/POSTGRES_PASSWORD=(\S+)/`, so a rewrite that drops the placeholder line reds a test in a different directory.
So this row EXTENDS an existing generated file with a NAMES-ONLY section; it does not create one, and it must not break the profile's own placeholder contract. Decide deliberately whether the required names go in the same file or an adjacent one, and say which and why.

CONCURRENCY WARNING: `controlled-profile-generator.ts` and its assets were being actively built by another session on 2026-09-05 (the ASSEMBLY HALF and the lockfile-asset mint). Re-measure at claim, expect the golden manifest hash to have moved, and never revert peer work.

NOT IN SCOPE: the plaintext delivery and the spawn merge (grandchild A); the Environments screen and the goal's unset count in the browser (the parent's child 3 - this row's report is a daemon-side read, not UI).

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`.
definitionOfDone: The required variable names are read from the APPROVED CONTRACT's deployment requirements (the field grandchild B added), never from a hand-kept list. Assert the read against a contract fixture carrying names, and assert that a contract with no names yields an empty required set rather than throwing.

A goal reports which required variables are UNSET for a given environment. Assert the exact unset SET for a goal with two required names where one is set - set equality, not toContain, and assert the SET one is absent from the report so the arm fails if the report simply echoes the requirement list.

`.env.example` carries every required NAME and NO VALUE for them. Assert the generated bytes contain each required name and that no required name is followed by a value; this file is committed and pushed through the repository, so a value here is a value published.

THE EXISTING PROFILE CONTRACT SURVIVES: the profile's own `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` placeholder is still present and still matches `/POSTGRES_PASSWORD=(\S+)/`, because apps/daemon/src/repository/deployment/deployment-infrastructure-generator.test.ts:305-306 reads it back. Assert it, and move the golden SHA256 pin at controlled-profile-generator.test.ts:32 to the new measured value rather than deleting the pin.

A contract with NO deployment-variable names generates the `.env.example` byte-identically to today - assert byte-identity, so this feature cannot change the profile for every project that does not use it.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: NAMES ONLY. `.env.example` is committed and pushed to the project's repository; a value written there is a value published. This is the single most common way this class of feature leaks.

EXTEND, DO NOT REPLACE, the existing generated `.env.example`. It already carries the profile's own placeholder, another directory's test reads that placeholder back, and a golden SHA256 pins the file.
MOVE THE GOLDEN PIN, NEVER DELETE IT. controlled-profile-generator.test.ts:32 pins .env.example by SHA256; re-measure and update the hash, and never soften the manifest to a looser assertion.
READ NAMES FROM THE APPROVED CONTRACT, never a hand-kept list - that is the whole point of grandchild B.
A PROJECT THAT NAMES NO VARIABLES MUST BE UNCHANGED, asserted as byte-identity of the generated file.
NO UI: the Environments screen and the browser's unset count are the parent's child 3.
